sources.locator: URL and application reputation checks; download history and prior results

sources.locator: First-, second-, third-party and government conformity-assessment roles
sources.supports: NIST distinguishes internal or first-party assessment, independent third-party assessment, and government's regulatory role.

sources.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
sources.locator: sections 2.4 and 3.2, Organizational Profiles and sector-specific implementation
sources.supports: CSF profiles let organizations tailor cybersecurity outcomes to sector, legal, regulatory, and business requirements.

sources.title: NIST: A Hierarchical Structure of Key Performance Indicators
sources.locator: p. 10, maintenance KPI Mean time to repair (MTTR)
sources.supports: NIST expands MTTR as Mean time to repair and treats it as a maintenance performance indicator.

sources.title: NIST: Timing Studies of Real-Time Linux for Control
sources.locator: Abstract; deterministic task execution for industrial control
sources.supports: Real-time operating systems support deterministic task execution for time-sensitive industrial control workloads.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-128: Security-Focused Configuration Management
sources.locator: sections 2.1 and 3.2, baseline configurations and configuration monitoring
sources.supports: Approved baseline configurations establish the secure build state; monitoring detects and addresses unauthorized drift.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-153: Guidelines for Securing Wireless Local Area Networks
sources.locator: Abstract and sections 2-3, WLAN radio communications and threats
sources.supports: WLAN security must address radio-range access, eavesdropping, rogue access points, and insecure wireless configurations.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1: Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems
sources.locator: sections 2.3 and 2.4, complexity, interactions, dependencies, and emergent behavior
sources.supports: System complexity grows through interacting components and dependencies and makes assurance and testing more difficult.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 Update 1: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
sources.locator: Abstract and executive summary; products, services, suppliers, counterfeit and malicious functionality
sources.supports: C-SCRM covers malicious, counterfeit, and vulnerable products and services introduced through supply-chain parties.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
sources.locator: Abstract and section 2, especially tenets 3 and 4
sources.supports: Zero trust protects individual resources and evaluates access before a session instead of trusting network location.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1: Contingency Planning Guide
sources.locator: section 5 and Appendix D, power failure and uninterruptible power supplies
sources.supports: Contingency planning treats power failure as a disruption and identifies UPS and alternate power as continuity measures.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53A Rev. 5: Assessing Security and Privacy Controls
sources.locator: chapter 3 and assessment procedures; assessor, method, object, and evidence
sources.supports: Control assessments use defined procedures and evidence to determine whether requirements are implemented and effective.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: Security and Privacy Controls
sources.locator: Control PE-3, Physical Access Control
sources.supports: PE-3 places guards and physical access devices within the physical-access-control family.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
sources.locator: Figure 3-1 and publication status
sources.supports: The superseded Rev. 2 grouped containment, eradication, and recovery as one lifecycle phase.

sources.locator: Publication metadata and section 2.1; final April 2025; supersedes Rev. 2
sources.supports: Rev. 3 is the current NIST incident-response publication and aligns incident response with CSF 2.0.

sources.locator: Abstract and section 2; OT, ICS, SCADA, PLC and embedded/real-time components
